title: How Drowning Works
summary: Josh Clark and Chuck Bryant explain how drowning works, starting with the larynx spasm and instinctive breath-holding, then how fresh and salt water affect the lungs and blood. They cover dry drowning and secondary (delayed) drowning, including the 2017 Texas case of Frankie Delgado, and describe the instinctive drowning response versus aquatic distress and how to spot a drowning person. The episode also covers rescue steps (CPR, mouth-to-mouth advice, recovery position), racial disparities in drowning rates, swimming lessons and prevention, drowning in bathtubs, hot tubs, and other household water hazards, and ends with listener mail about a Steve Miller Band lyric and Marshall Tucker Band flute.

entities.name: Contested Waters: A Social History of Swimming Pools in America

segments.title: Opening banter and what drowning is not
segments.summary: The hosts open by saying drowning is not peaceful, referencing survivor accounts. They discuss the 2002 World Congress of Drowning's universal definition and the misconception that drowning equals death.

segments.title: Physiology: larynx spasm, hypoxemia, and water in the lungs
segments.summary: The process begins when water contacts the larynx, which spasms and closes. Oxygen falls and carbon dioxide rises until the body forces a breath, usually after about 80-some seconds. Water in the lungs then damages surfactant in the alveoli, with freshwater destroying it and saltwater washing it away, and the blood becomes diluted or concentrated.

segments.title: Dry drowning and secondary drowning
segments.summary: Dry drowning refers to deaths where the larynx spasmed and the person asphyxiated without water entering the lungs; the CDC and others call this drowning. Secondary drowning is delayed death after water was inhaled. The 2017 Texas case of Frankie Delgado, a four-year-old who died days after a wave incident, is described, with warning signs such as lethargy and vomiting.

segments.title: Instinctive drowning response and recognizing drowning
segments.summary: Aquatic distress is loud splashing and yelling and is not necessarily drowning. Francesco Pia defined the quiet instinctive drowning response, in which the victim cannot call for help, uses only the arms, and may appear vertical with head low and eyes closed. Many children drown near a supervising adult who does not recognize it.

segments.title: Rescue and treatment
segments.summary: For a pool drowning, send someone for help and get a defibrillator, then assess breathing and pulse. The American Heart Association advises mouth-to-mouth alongside chest compressions for drowning, unlike hands-only CPR. Keep the neck supported because of possible injury, and roll an unconscious breathing person onto their side. The hosts discuss rock stars who died from aspiration of vomit.

segments.title: Racial disparities and swimming lessons
segments.summary: Black and Native American and Alaska Native people drown at higher rates than white people, with African American children aged 11 to 12 drowning in pools about ten times the white rate. Historical segregation limited pool access, and the lack of swimming lessons has passed down through families. Swimming lessons help but do not drown-proof a person.

segments.title: Home water hazards and child supervision
segments.summary: Hosts give prevention tips: touch supervision for small children, fencing pools, having CPR training and a landline by the pool, and watching a child after a close call. Infants can drown in an inch of water such as a dog bowl or bucket. Bathtub and hot tub drownings among adults are discussed, including Whitney Houston and Orville Redenbacher, and car drownings in Florida.

segments.title: Listener mail: Steve Miller Band and Marshall Tucker Band
segments.summary: A listener shares a story about the Steve Miller Band lyric about peaches. Another anecdote describes a Marshall Tucker Band flute player met in a store.

segments.title: Sign-off
segments.summary: The hosts close the episode and give social media and email contact information.
